# Family History Research Planning for Muse

A methodology-first companion for family history: its core rule is plan before searching — when you mention an ancestor, it gathers what you already know, defines the research question, and builds a structured research plan (objectives, FAN-principle strategy, prioritized sources, timeline, success criteria) before any search happens. Beyond planning it generates Evidence Explained–style citations for 14+ record types, runs a seven-step evidence analysis and conflict-resolution framework (source inventory, reliability ranking, comparison matrix, GPS compliance check, proof argument with proof levels), and keeps disciplined research logs of every session, including negative results. Ships with ready-to-use templates (research plan, citation library, evidence analysis, research log) and deep references on citation templates, evidence evaluation, research strategies, and GPS guidelines. Discovered via skills.sh. Honest note: this is a planning and methodology skill — it structures and documents your research rather than finding ancestors for you, and execution only proceeds on your explicit request. It complements rather than duplicates the genealogy research-partner skill: use this one to plan, that one to dig. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use. Not verified.
